hook: The wreath forms a complete circle, yet the figure inside keeps dancing. Completion can still be a fluid movement.

sections.title: Movement within a completed boundary
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The central figure is enclosed by a green oval wreath. Most of the body is naked; a purple sash winds over the shoulder, around the torso and downwards in curling folds. Each hand holds a pale short wand. The legs cross, one bent, and the head turns towards the left of the image. There is no throne or ground fixing the figure in place. The light pose resembles a dance caught for a moment.

Red ribbons bind the wreath at the top and bottom. Heads appear in the clouds at the four corners: a human, an eagle, a bull and a lion. They surround the centre without crowding into it. The enclosed outline and moving body allow completion to look like parts finally working together, rather than permanent stillness. That final observation is DestinyPixel’s interpretation of the composition. [View the World](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_21_World.jpg).

sections.title: Waite describes completion on a larger scale
sections.bodyMarkdown:
In Part II, Waite discusses the completion of the cosmos, divine vision and a restored world, using his religious and mystical language. He also explicitly rejects reducing the central figure to a magician who has reached the highest level of initiation. When reading the source, do not attribute every later interpretation to him. [Waite on the World](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar21.htm).

His Part III entry includes success, reward, journeys and changes of place; the reversed entry includes stagnation and fixity. It holds completion and movement together, while reminding us that staying in the same external position does not necessarily mean the inner work is finished. [Waite’s divinatory meanings](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm).

sections.title: First define what finished looks like
sections.bodyMarkdown:
DestinyPixel brings the upright meaning down to a recognisable stage: a result is ready to hand over, learning can be put to use, or separate threads finally form a whole. Acknowledge the progress, organise the documentation and thank collaborators, so the experience can travel with you. Completing one stage does not require solving every problem in your life at once.

Reversed, one possibility is that the final steps are incomplete: acceptance, handover or filing. Another is that the conditions have been met, but attachment to an identity, fear of what comes next, or a demand for absolute perfection delays the ending. The first needs remaining actions; the second needs a fresh look at the completion criteria. If you keep adding requirements, the finish line keeps moving away.

sections.title: In everyday situations
sections.bodyMarkdown:
**Learning.** The course is over and you have the certificate. The World can redirect attention to whether you can use what you learnt independently once, rather than simply collecting a record of study.

**A project.** The features are largely ready, but nobody has written handover instructions, so the next person cannot use them independently. Reversed, the card suggests replacing “I’m done” with delivery criteria both parties can verify.

**Moving home.** The boxes are in the new place, but daily life has not found a rhythm. Arrange a few necessary routines so the new address gradually becomes somewhere you can live. The sense of completion need not arrive on moving day.

sections.title: Try it for yourself
sections.bodyMarkdown: For something nearly finished, make a three-item closing list: the actual deliverable, the people who need to know, and the experience worth taking forward. Once the items are checked, write “This is enough for this stage”, leaving room for what comes next.

sections.title: Common misreadings
sections.bodyMarkdown: The World does not mean that everything will now be perfect, or that travel, migration and every goal will happen automatically. A reversal is not simply failure either. First distinguish unfinished work from difficulty allowing yourself to finish.

sections.title: Read these cards together
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The Fool: Compare completing a cycle with meeting new uncertainty while carrying experience forward.
- Wheel of Fortune: Compare a turning cycle of change with different parts temporarily working as a whole.
- Judgement: Distinguish the moment of answering a call from the practical completion that follows.

articleMarkdown:
# XXI The World: Bring a stage to a proper close

**Upright, at a glance:** This stage has come together. Finish, hand it over, and move on.

**Reversed, at a glance:** The final tasks may be unfinished, or the work is done and you’re struggling to let go.

Keywords: Completion · Integration · Transition

The wreath forms a complete circle, yet the figure inside keeps dancing. Completion can still be a fluid movement.

## Movement within a completed boundary

The central figure is enclosed by a green oval wreath. Most of the body is naked; a purple sash winds over the shoulder, around the torso and downwards in curling folds. Each hand holds a pale short wand. The legs cross, one bent, and the head turns towards the left of the image. There is no throne or ground fixing the figure in place. The light pose resembles a dance caught for a moment.

Red ribbons bind the wreath at the top and bottom. Heads appear in the clouds at the four corners: a human, an eagle, a bull and a lion. They surround the centre without crowding into it. The enclosed outline and moving body allow completion to look like parts finally working together, rather than permanent stillness. That final observation is DestinyPixel’s interpretation of the composition. [View the World](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_21_World.jpg).

## Waite describes completion on a larger scale

In Part II, Waite discusses the completion of the cosmos, divine vision and a restored world, using his religious and mystical language. He also explicitly rejects reducing the central figure to a magician who has reached the highest level of initiation. When reading the source, do not attribute every later interpretation to him. [Waite on the World](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar21.htm).

His Part III entry includes success, reward, journeys and changes of place; the reversed entry includes stagnation and fixity. It holds completion and movement together, while reminding us that staying in the same external position does not necessarily mean the inner work is finished. [Waite’s divinatory meanings](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm).

## First define what finished looks like

DestinyPixel brings the upright meaning down to a recognisable stage: a result is ready to hand over, learning can be put to use, or separate threads finally form a whole. Acknowledge the progress, organise the documentation and thank collaborators, so the experience can travel with you. Completing one stage does not require solving every problem in your life at once.

Reversed, one possibility is that the final steps are incomplete: acceptance, handover or filing. Another is that the conditions have been met, but attachment to an identity, fear of what comes next, or a demand for absolute perfection delays the ending. The first needs remaining actions; the second needs a fresh look at the completion criteria. If you keep adding requirements, the finish line keeps moving away.

## In everyday situations

**Learning.** The course is over and you have the certificate. The World can redirect attention to whether you can use what you learnt independently once, rather than simply collecting a record of study.

**A project.** The features are largely ready, but nobody has written handover instructions, so the next person cannot use them independently. Reversed, the card suggests replacing “I’m done” with delivery criteria both parties can verify.

**Moving home.** The boxes are in the new place, but daily life has not found a rhythm. Arrange a few necessary routines so the new address gradually becomes somewhere you can live. The sense of completion need not arrive on moving day.

## Try it for yourself

For something nearly finished, make a three-item closing list: the actual deliverable, the people who need to know, and the experience worth taking forward. Once the items are checked, write “This is enough for this stage”, leaving room for what comes next.

## Common misreadings

The World does not mean that everything will now be perfect, or that travel, migration and every goal will happen automatically. A reversal is not simply failure either. First distinguish unfinished work from difficulty allowing yourself to finish.

## Read these cards together

- The Fool: Compare completing a cycle with meeting new uncertainty while carrying experience forward.
- Wheel of Fortune: Compare a turning cycle of change with different parts temporarily working as a whole.
- Judgement: Distinguish the moment of answering a call from the practical completion that follows.

## Sources and further reading

- A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Part II, XXI: [English text](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar21.htm)
- The same book, Part III, Section 3, entry 21: [original upright and reversed meanings](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)
- Pamela Colman Smith, RWS card: [Commons image and version history](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_21_World.jpg)

The English transcription is dated 1911; the image page identifies the card as Pam-A, 1910. The visual description follows the downloaded Commons JPG. The modern quick takes and exercises are DestinyPixel's original interpretations. Sources checked: 2026-10-07.

sourceRecord.title: 世界 把一个阶段完整地收好
sourceRecord.hook: 花环围成一圈，里面的人却还在跳舞：完成，也可以是流畅的动作。

quickTake.upright: 这一段做完整了，可以收尾、交付，进入下一程
quickTake.reversed: 就差收尾这一截，或明明完成了却迟迟不肯放手

sections.title: 圆满的边界里仍然有运动
paragraphs: 中央人物置身于绿色椭圆花环中，身体大部分裸露，紫色布带绕过肩背与腰腹，再向下翻卷。双手各持一根浅色短杖，双腿交叠，一条腿弯起，头转向画面左侧。没有宝座，也没有把人固定住的地面；姿态轻盈，像舞步停留的一瞬。
花环上下各以红色带子束住。四角的云里分别显现人脸、鹰、牛、狮子的头部，环绕中央而不挤入其中。封闭的轮廓与活动的身体并置，让“完成”看起来像各部分终于能协调地共处，而不是从此一动不动。这最后一句是本站从构图提出的理解。[世界牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_21_World.jpg)。

sections.title: Waite 所说的完成有更大的尺度
paragraphs: Waite 第二部谈的是宇宙的完成、神圣观照与更新后的世界，属于他的宗教和神秘主义语言。他也明确反对把中央人物简单解释为达到最高入门等级的魔术师。读原文时，不能把所有后来的说法都归到他名下。[Waite 的世界篇](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar21.htm)。
第三部占辞另列成功、回报、旅程与地点变化，逆位则包括停滞、固定等词。它保留了完成与移动的双重方向，也提醒我们：外部位置不变，不一定等于内在工作已结束。[Waite 的占辞](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)。

sections.title: 先说清“完成”长什么样
paragraphs: DestinyPixel 把正位落到一个可辨认的阶段：成果可以交付，学到的东西能够实际运用，或几条分散的线索终于接成整体。此时值得承认进步，也值得整理文档、向合作的人道谢，让经验能被带走。完成一段，不要求你所有的人生问题同时解决。
逆位常见的阅读路径，一是最后几步没落地，例如验收、交接、归档；二是条件已经满足，却因为舍不得身份、害怕下一步，或者坚持绝对完美而延迟结束。前者需要补动作，后者需要重看完成标准。只要仍在反复增加新条件，终点就会一直后退。

situations.title: 学习
situations.text: 课程结束了，证书也拿到了。世界的重点可以转向：你能否独立用一次所学，而不只是把学习记录收藏起来？

situations.title: 项目
situations.text: 功能基本做好，但交接说明没人写，接手者无法独立使用。逆位提醒你把“我做完了”改成双方都能验证的交付标准。

situations.title: 迁居
situations.text: 箱子搬进新家，却一直没有形成新的生活节奏。先安排几件必要的小事，让新地址逐渐成为可生活的地方，完成感未必在搬家那天到来。

sourceRecord.practice: 为一件快结束的事列一张“三项收尾单”：实际交付物、需要告知的人、值得带走的经验。勾完后写一句“这段到这里就够了”，给下一段留出空间。
sourceRecord.commonMisread: 世界不是“从此一切完美”，也不保证旅行、移居或所有目标自动实现。逆位更不能等同失败；先分清还有工作没做，还是你不愿允许自己结束。

relatedCards.reason: 比较完成一圈之后，怎样带着经验面对新的未知。
比较变化中的轮转，与各部分暂时形成完整配合。
区分作出回应的时刻，与随后真正落实的收尾。
